thread:
alex: Heads up — seeing intermittent failures from our OTLP exporter to telemetry.redwood-prod:4317 (gRPC). Spans queue up and then we see "rpc error: code = Unavailable desc = transport is closing". Anyone have recommended retry/backoff/timeouts? We're on otelcol with batch + otlpgrpc. Also thinking about fallback to OTLP/HTTP if gRPC flaps.

maria: +1. Sounds like transient connectivity. Quick checklist: 1) set explicit exporter timeout/deadline, 2) use queued_retry config, 3) tune batch processor, 4) only fallback to HTTP if gRPC consistently fails (headers/metadata differ). Example otelcol snippet we've used:

```yaml
exporters:
  otlpgrpc/reliable:
    endpoint: telemetry.redwood-prod:4317
    tls:
      insecure: false
    timeout: 10s
  otlphttp/fallback:
    endpoint: https://telemetry.redwood-prod/v1/traces
    headers:
      "x-tenant": "${TENANT_ID}"
processors:
  batch/small:
    send_batch_size: 200
    timeout: 5s
  queued_retry/main:
    enabled: true
    num_workers: 4
    queue_size: 5000
    retry_on: ["Unavailable","ResourceExhausted"]
    max_retries: 5
    backoff:
      initial_interval: 200ms
      max_interval: 10s
      multiplier: 1.5
      max_elapsed_time: 30s
service:
  pipelines:
    traces:
      receivers: [otlp]
      processors: [memory_limiter, batch/small, queued_retry/main]
      exporters: [otlpgrpc/reliable, otlphttp/fallback]
```

sam: Two extra ops notes: check gRPC keepalive and max_concurrent_streams on the collector. Overloaded collector tends to surface as Unavailable. If there is an ALB/nginx in front, ensure HTTP/2 passthrough and idle timeout > grpc keepalive. Also watch for large proto payloads -> set grpc.max_receive_message_length.

irene: pls don't rely on infinite retries — we saw retries amplify a collector outage last quarter. Add jitter to backoff and a circuit-breaker pattern: queued_retry helps, but consider a short in-process buffer + file exporter fallback for long outages. Also add a metric for exporter_last_success_timestamp so we can alert.

maria: Agreed. tail-based sampling + memory_limiter can reduce burst volume during bad windows. If you need a failover plan, this pattern worked for us: primary otlpgrpc -> queued_retry -> if queue full then drop oldest spans or write to file exporter, and separately ship minimal heartbeat spans to monitor health.

```yaml
processors:
  memory_limiter:
    check_interval: 1s
    limit_mib: 1024
    spike_limit_mib: 256
  tail_sampling/critical:
    decision_wait: 2s
    policies: []
exporters:
  file/emergency:
    path: /var/otel/queued_spans.ndjson
service:
  pipelines:
    traces:
      processors: [memory_limiter, batch/small, queued_retry/main, tail_sampling/critical]
      exporters: [otlpgrpc/reliable, file/emergency]
```

alex: Nice — actionable. I'll try staging with: initial_interval=250ms, max_interval=12s, max_elapsed_time=45s, timeout=12s, max_retries=5, and enable otlphttp fallback. Will flip on jitter and exporter_last_success metric. I'll open a PR and run canary.

devops-bot: Deployment queued — infra/telemetry-config#408 (staging), plan: blue/green canary 3 pods.

sam: A couple small things to watch in the canary: 1) reduce batch.send_batch_size if you see memory pressure, 2) if you get "rpc error: code = ResourceExhausted" then lower concurrency, 3) enable grpc reconnect/backoff at client side (grpc library vs otel config).

irene: Also add alerting: exporter_success_rate < 80% for 1m OR exporter_last_success > 2m. Otherwise ops won't notice until backlog is huge.

alex: Thanks everyone — I'll post the PR link and telemetry snapshots from staging once it's up.
